utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. Cross-examination continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. Before I continue with my cross-examination, I would like to inform the Court that the Prosecution has just provided me with the official translation and the statement given at the SUP and also the ruling of the Court. So now I do have the official translation of the document D23/3 ter ID and 24/3 ter ID. So I don't know, now should I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to confirm with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Those documents were provided to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to introduce first document D23 ter ID, the English version. And could the usher please distribute the copies to members of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, our notes indicate that this is document D22/3. I just want to clarify with the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. The registry assistant, please can you help with the correct number? This is the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The English translation is the translation of document D22/3 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And which one is this one? What is it, the D22?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the statement given at the SUP in Bosanski Samac on the 9th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The one the witness had said yesterday that he didn't -- it wasn't his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the other document is 24/3, according to our records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: D -- the judgement indictment -- judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, the judgement of the court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I just wanted to clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is the English translation of document D24/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. Today we will continue with a few more questions. I think I will be brief, but I would also ask you, like I did before, just to respond with "yes," "no," "I don't know." If you don't understand my question, you can ask for it to be repeated so that we don't have problems like we did yesterday about interpretation of the question. Before we move to a different topic, I just want to come back briefly to some of your responses yesterday regarding the distribution of weapons in the courtyard of the TO building. Something there is not quite clear to me. Yesterday, in response to my question, you said that you don't know who it was who decided who would be distributed weapons, who would receive weapons and who wouldn't. Immediately after that, you responded to my question whether you had asked to receive weapons, that you didn't ask for that because you were sure that you wouldn't have received a weapon. These two things are not quite logical to me. You're sure that you would not have received a weapon, but you don't know who made these decisions. Could you clarify this for us a little bit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that I wouldn't have received a weapon from those people whom I had seen there, because they knew I was Tota's brother, and they knew my brothers were in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is clear to me but previously I asked you who it was who was issuing the weapons and you said you didn't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the people who were there at the TO headquarters, the large door, the gate was open, and I could see these people, Milos Bogdanovic, Marko Bozanovic, Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Milos Bogdanovic was working at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was commander of the headquarters of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go to the courtyard of the TO building out of curiosity or you went because you wanted to receive a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went more out of curiosity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume that your memory serves you well, at least in regard to what you stated one month ago, and I will remind you what you said. On December 3rd, before this same Trial Chamber, on page 5016, you responded as follows, I will read it in English [In English]: "My fellow citizens carrying rifles so I went there too." [Interpretation] And after that, you stated, on page 5017: [English]: "I saw many people carrying weapons, and I thought why shouldn't I have one too." [Interpretation] You said this on the 3rd of December. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ye.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you again: Did you go there in order to receive a rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I set out towards the TO headquarters, I knew that they wouldn't give me a weapon, but I went to see it. I went to see who was distributing and who was being issued with the weapons. I was more interested in that. Regarding my statement from December 3rd, I completely agree. I could see that Serbian families were leaving Samac. They were fleeing. So I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more clarification regarding the responses you gave yesterday. When I asked you about your (redacted), you told me that he worked in the offices with Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was (redacted) involved or working on the exchanges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he worked on them. I'm sure, though, that this didn't go through him. Perhaps he compiled the lists on orders from others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sveto Vasovic work on the exchanges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also in the offices with Mr. Tadic, with (redacted) .

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We won't ask any more questions about that topic. I would like to now deal with another part of your statement from the month of December for clarification. On the 7th of December when you were interviewed by the Prosecution, on page 5250, you stated that the wife of Avdo Drljacic paid 400 marks, German marks to Miroslav Tadic so that he would put Avdo on the list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You knew Avdo Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Avdo was with you at the Batkovic camp; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when Avdo Drljacic was exchanged, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: August or September of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have different information, but I want to ask you anyway. Are you sure it was summer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you're not sure, well, I will tell you. The information I have is that Avdo Drljacic was exchanged on the 24th of December, 1992. Is it possible that he was exchanged at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please bear with me for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In any event, he was exchanged quite awhile before you were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see him and his wife after you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1994, in the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who told you that Avdo's wife gave that money to Tadic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, counsel. I just want to remind you to be switching off the microphone after you ask the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you respond, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: His wife was exchanged at the same time that my wife was exchanged in 1993, and Avdo was also exchanged at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you who told you about that money.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife told me first. She told me, "If I had had the money, I would have gotten you out as well."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who told her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she was together with Avdo's wife Fadila in the bus. My wife and Avdo's wife, they were exchanged together on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked -- I didn't ask you who she was exchanged with. I asked you who told your wife that Avdo's wife gave the money to Tadic. So can you please answer to that? Was that -- was that Avdo's wife who told you or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Avdo's wife told my wife and my wife told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I just consult with my client for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me the wife -- the name of Avdo Drljaca's wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadila.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They had two children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is the real name of Avdo Drljacic Abdulah Drljacic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him as Avdo. I don't know his real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he born in 1958?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like the witness to be shown two exchange lists. Unfortunately, at the moment I don't have enough copies to be able to introduce that into evidence, but these are the lists of people who were exchanged on the 24th of December, 1992, when Abdulah Drljacic was exchanged and when his wife and two children were exchanged. This is evidence of the Prosecution, Number 00734804. And I would just like the witness to look at this list of women to see whether his wife was exchanged at the same time as the wife of Abdulah Drljacic, and perhaps during the break I will be able to make enough copies so that I could tender that -- the list into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I wanted to be clear, because you said this is evidence of the Prosecution. So I'm wondering what document that is. Then it should have a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The list of the men, I do have the number of Prosecution evidence, but the list of the women, perhaps I'm not sure if this is a document that I received from the Prosecution, but I'm not ready at this point to tender it into evidence. The Prosecution is in any case familiar with both of these lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All I'm wondering is it hasn't been discussed in this case before. It hasn't got an ID number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. And both documents are in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, just the list of exchanges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I hear from the Prosecution? MR. DI FAZIO: I'm in a difficult position because I haven't seen the document, and I don't know which of our documents it supposedly is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the usher can get the document from counsel and show it to the Prosecution counsel. MR. DI FAZIO: I wonder if Mr. Lukic can tell us if it is one of the documents in on your 65 ter list. We had a series of lists of exchanges and it may be one of those, in which case --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One is from that list. One is from that document; the other is not. MR. DI FAZIO: Just for the sake of -- of efficiency, can we just have them marked at this stage and then I can consider -- look at them carefully and provide the Chamber with my attitude towards the question of its form --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have them given to the registry assistant for marking them with ID numbers. MR. DI FAZIO: The copies I have or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. I only have those ones now. I'll make a copy during the break. MR. DI FAZIO: I do apologise. I wonder for the assistance of the Prosecution whether Mr. Lukic could indicate which of the exchange lists, which document it is so we that can probably -- dig out our own copies as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So one document which have a number of the copy of number of Prosecutor 734802. It's the list of the exchanged persons, men. First person on that list named Drljacic, Abdulah. Just the best --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the ID number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: ID number is document D25/3 ter ID, and the next document D26/3 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown document D26/3. So only that one. MR. DI FAZIO: Might I see the document just very briefly before it's handed to the witness, just cast my eye over it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness should be shown D26 first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, I don't believe you have ever seen this document before. I would like to ask you to read the heading of the document slowly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: "List of civilians who went for exchange on the 21st of December, 1992, in Dragalic."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this list consists mostly of women and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are also some elderly men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you look at this list, I think it has only two pages.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please have a look to see if you can find the wife of Avdo Drljacic on this list, and if so, under what number, and also whether your wife's name is on the list. If you see your wife's name, don't say it out loud, but simply tell us whether she's on the list or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 79, that's Avdo's mother, and under number 84 is his wife and two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you have a look again to see whether your wife and children are on this list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will ask you again. Did Avdo's wife tell your wife, in the summer of 1993, on the bus as we were being exchanged, that she had given money to Tadic? Think carefully.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife was exchanged on the 27th of January, 1993. That is the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But let me remind you of what you just said, that Avdo Drljacic's wife was in the same exchange. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this list no, but I wasn't there at that exchange because Mr. Tadic would to the hangar, read out names from the list, people would go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you still assert that Avdo Drljacic's wife was exchanged at the same time as yours and that that was when she had told her that she had given money to Tadic? Is that what you're saying or not? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told you what my wife told me, because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You also told me that you saw Avdo Drljacic afterwards, after your release.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many times did you see him, if I can ask you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost every day. We lived in the same street in Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he ever tell you that his wife had given money to Tadic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did she tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me that on several occasions. He always used to say, "One should have money in one's pocket. If you would have had some money, you would have been released."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you haven't answer my question. Did he tell you that his wife had given money to Tadic, yes or no, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, the date when he told you that, approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in 1994, maybe in July or August. Because we were neighbours, and we would sit down together more than once.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he was exchanged together with his wife, that is, his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that when I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, you gave your first statement to the OTP investigators in June 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you were asked about the alleged payments made to Tadic for putting names on the exchange lists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And at that time, you never mentioned Avdo Drljacic and his wife; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly what I said in 1996 because I have made so many statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to read your statement to you and remind you that there is no mention of Avdo Drljacic in it, are you certain? Can you confirm this? Can you confirm that you did not mention Avdo Drljacic in 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were interviewed a second time by the Prosecutor in the summer of last year in Orasje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in Gradacac the second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion, you never mentioned Avdo Drljacic and his wife, and yet Tadic was discussed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first time you mentioned Avdo Drljacic's wife was here during your proofing sessions in December with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should know that I was not in a hotel those two years. I was in a camp. Things come back to me. I couldn't remember everything all at once, all the things I'd been through.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that your memory was fresher in 1996 than it is -- it was in 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. One grows old.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that Avdo Drljacic made a statement to investigators of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to ask you just a few more questions in connection with your statement. Do you -- have you ever been to Samac since your release?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me how often you've been there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I have some time off, when I'm free on Sundays.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you go to cafes in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I go to Ignjo Popovic's place because he's a school friend of mine. So that's the only place I go to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that you mention Ignjo Popovic, did your schoolmate tell you that he had taken some people away from Samac, transported them away from Samac during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, because I wasn't in Samac during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see any of the people we have heard about, Cera, do you see them in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see Perica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see Mr. Blagovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in Gradacac once, then Stojan Blagovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Marinko Stefanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to ask just a few more questions about the topic that we started yesterday and that's the statement made in the SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, since yesterday, you have had time to look at the text of the statement in full. With reference to the facts you spoke of before this Court, is there anything in this statement that contradicts what you said? Yes or no? If there is, tell us what.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I object to that question. It's enormously general and completely unspecific. What is he supposed to do? Revise everything that he said and then compare it with this? I don't mind my learned friend putting contradictions to him, it's perfectly proper, but it's got to be specific. He's got to know what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but this is the statement to which the witness said he didn't sign. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Isn't this the same statement that he was allowed to take with him so that he could read through and see whether or not -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- he made it, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I've got no problems with his being asked about the content of the statement. Indeed he should be, because we're still uncertain as to whether he is the author of this or -- all that we know so far is he says that's not my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: We don't even know what he says about the rest of the document. It seems to me that if my learned friend wants to cross-examine him about that, I've got no objection, but we've got to see what the witness says about the content of the document, so he can say, "It's mine," or, "No, it's not mine," and then -- and then put contradictions to him if Mr. Lukic thinks that he's contradicted himself. That should be the procedure rather than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because -- yes, because you can only put a contradiction from a statement if the witness says he made the statement. MR. DI FAZIO: That's right. Now if he says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because it's possible that he could have given a statement but never signed it. That's possible. MR. DI FAZIO: That's possible. I entirely agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: That's exactly right. But until he says, "Look, I've looked at the content of the statement, and I can say it's mine or I can say it's not mine," that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That has to be established -- MR. DI FAZIO: That has to be established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and then we can go into the contents. But before that is done -- Mr. Lukic, I'm sure you're following the submissions of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but I think that as regards the content of the statement, my question is quite proper. I just wanted to know whether there is anything in this document that is not correct. If we are to go sentence by sentence, part by part, I can do that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. But we have to know -- you should ask the witness whether he made this statement. He may not have signed it; it is possible. So we have to clear that first before we can deal with contradictions, if any.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I asked the witness yesterday and he responding to the question and the question of my learned friend he said that he had never signed a statement, and to my question of yesterday he also said he didn't sign it, so I will ask again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have read this statement in detail. Are you still saying that this is not your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is not correct. When I was discussing with the Prosecution, I did say it is possible for a person under interrogation to make a statement, right, and yet not sign it, he just goes or he is released, right? It is possible. So if you ask him -- because he read it through. First you ask him whether he made the statement, which is recorded in this document, because he could have made it and yet still say he didn't sign it, and then you can deal with the contradictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, Judge Mumba. I asked the witness yesterday. I asked him many questions regarding his statement to the SUP before I showed him the document, and then he said that specifically he responded to the questions to Inspector Savic only whether he was or was not a member of the SDA scouts unit, and now I will ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Besides that fact, did you say anything else to Inspector Savic during your questioning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inspector Savic showed me a red piece of paper written by hand about this size where there was my name, stating that I was a member of the scout unit. After I told him that I was not a scout, he was continually holding a police baton. He kept bending it and hitting it on the table. But he didn't take any notes. He didn't write anything down. But I don't remember. And he didn't give me anything to sign either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So he didn't ask you anything about your membership in the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This top part of the statement, he asked me right away when I was at the door whether I was in the SDA. The second part of the statement, when I was detained the first time, around the 12th of April, then the officer on duty, Mirko Pavic, when Cera brought me to the SUP, when I ran to the SUP, then he went and checked and said, "There's nothing against you. Go home and don't go out." And then after three or four months, when I was detained, Stevan Arandjic appeared and saying that I wounded him in April. So this is September now, so it's practically four months or longer that this stayed there. Stevan didn't report me that I wounded him. I walked around Samac freely. I was walking. I was carrying out my work duty, and I was close to the police station every day. Nobody brought me in or arrested me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you on the first day to be specific and if you don't remember something to say that you don't remember it. My question yesterday was -- this was also a question asked to you by my learned friend the Prosecutor, decidedly whether the investigator Milos Savic asked you anything else except about your membership in the SDA scouts units, and you responded no. Now we hear that when you were at the door, as you said, he did ask you about whether you were a member of the SDA or not. Did you remember this when you read this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last night, when I was reading the document, I remembered a little bit, the bit about the SDA. But I think that when you asked me before about the police officer, you asked me that yesterday. And also about whether I was at the roadblocks or at the barricades. This -- that part fits.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we can agree that Inspector Savic, during your questioning in the SUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your microphone, please, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The witness is describing two different interviews; one at the door of the police station, and one when he's interviewed apparently upon or after arrest, and now they're trying to mix them together. He's talking about two separate interviews and then trying to say that he's being either incorrect or he's not being truthful with the Court, or he's confused. There's two separate interviews which occurred apparently. One was at the door of the police where a couple of questions were asked, and one was at a later point, and then there's kind of the third at Batanice which was some sort of a trial, if you want to refer to it even as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. Can we have clearer questioning, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not making any insinuations. If my question was not clear to my learned friend from the Prosecution, he will have the opportunity in redirect to re-establish this again. I asked the witness, and I thought he understood me, whether Milos Savic right away asked him at the door to the room where he was conducting the interview, asked him about his membership in the SDA, and also about all of these facts that are noted in the statement except for those related to Stevo Arandjic. So this is just one statement. Is this one statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This top part of the statement about membership in the SDA, I didn't see a pen or a pencil in his hand, and there was nothing for me to sign. He only had one small piece of red paper and that was all. I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: See then we can agree that you told Inspector Milos Savic, when you were giving him your statement -- so you gave him information about your membership in the SDA, about your leaving the SDA, about your conflict with Coner, about your alibi, we can put it that way, in the time when the barricades, roadblocks were put up, but you claim that you didn't say anything regarding Stevo Arandjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, again I'm not objecting to the question, but -- sorry, the line of questioning here, but there's a whole heap of topics that my learned friend has put to this witness as apparently contained in what we call the first part of the statement. We've got information about membership of the SDA, leaving the SDA, conflict with Coner, alibi because of the roadblocks, but nothing about Stevo Arandjic, and he answers "Yes." Now, how are you -- how will you know if the witness is saying he's merely agreeing nothing about Stevo Arandjic and whether or not the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. witness is agreeing that all those other discreet little topics were in fact in reality put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think the -- yes. The points that the counsel mentioned, the topics of interview -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- were clear and the witness answered. That's all that counsel did. Counsel is not saying everything in this statement. No, he pointed out the topics. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I've got no problem with that. I've got no problem with that. But I don't know if the witness is agreeing that all of those topics were raised or merely that Arandjic was mentioned. I don't know and how can the Chamber know that. If I might respectfully suggest, what Mr. Lukic should do is put to him one by one. During that interview was membership in the SDA mentioned, yes or no. And the witness can say -- tell us. Then go on and tell us was Coner mentioned, your conflict with him, yes or no, and then we can go on. And then finally get to that point, because you just don't know whether the witness is agreeing that all of these things in the first part of the statement were in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. MR. DI FAZIO: -- put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What I'm saying is the topics discussed by counsel were clear, right, as to what was discussed between the witness and the person who was interrogating him. So the counsel -- counsel isn't saying they're all in this statement. He has left the statement aside. He's merely picking out the topics. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we can go through this again just to make it clear, because it seems to me you wanted the questions put to the witness one by one. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I think that would be clear so that we can know whether or not those topics were raised in fact with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: With the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: -- at the interview. I know not in regards to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The statement, no. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps I misunderstood it, I don't know. But it seemed to me we were left with some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Maybe -- MR. DI FAZIO: I think it would be important to the Defence counsel, I would think, if he's going to eventually submit that the document is true or false. From that point of view, I think we should be absolutely sure about just what was said between this witness and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- and the interrogator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think Mr. Lukic have very easily go over that again one question at a time and then the witness can give the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume, sir, you understood what we are about to clarify. I will ask you questions now and you will respond. During your questioning in November 1992 at the SUP premises by Inspector Milos Savic, at that time, did you say anything about your membership in the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this was in September and not November, and I said about my membership in the SDA just as it is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you tell Inspector Savic anything about the reasons why you left the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it's written here, the conflicts, these are the reasons which I talked about, which I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you told him that you had a dispute with Coner and that that is the reason why you left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you, on that occasion, answer about questions about your alleged presence at the roadblocks, i.e., were you present at the roadblocks that were set up by the members of the SDA in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The inspector had photographs of people who were at the roadblocks, and he only asked me where I was at the time the roadblocks were set up, and I told him where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please concentrate on the statement first and go back to the road blocks later. Try to establish and get on with this document first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am asking the witness facts from the document. It's the last sentence in the first paragraph, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You haven't highlighted that, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Singh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You didn't highlight that. You want to expand your inquiry now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I highlighted in yellow thinking that yesterday we would just read parts of the statement. So I just wanted the relevant parts of the statement to be read out. But now since the witness has read the whole statement, I'm asking you him about all the facts that he talked about in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, on that occasion you told Inspector Savic that you were at the Hotel Plaza with Gligorovic and Tutnjevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you talk -- did you tell Inspector Savic on that occasion and did he question you about whether you would a member of the SDA scouts unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He showed me a list of 10 or 11 people on a piece of paper where there was also my name and my phone number. I denied this categorically because I was not a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did I understand properly that at that time you told the Inspector that you were not a member of the scouts unit of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Inspector Savic ask you anything regarding the incident with Stevo Arandjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've read this statement. You also read that part of the statement last night; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This statement from the 9th of November, 1992, the part that relates to Stevo Arandjic, is that in any way different compared to what you told the court in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave the same statement to the court in Bijeljina and to the public security station in Samac, that I did not have a weapon, so therefore, I was not able to wound him. And I only heard about Stevo Arandjic at the court in Bijeljina. Before that, I didn't even know about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we please clarify something? You have just said that before the court in Bijeljina and in the public security station in Samac, you said that you didn't have a weapon and that you could not have wounded him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. How -- with what could I have wounded him? If I was at home, sitting at home, I was taken away, beaten. I was carrying out my work duty. How could I have wounded him? With what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you tell that to Inspector Savic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's what it says here, that I did not have a firearm. It's written here, but I didn't even say that. We didn't talk about Stevan Arandjic in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, a few minutes ago, you stated: [Previous translation continues]... "statement to the court in Bijeljina and to the public security station in Samac that he did not have weapon. So therefore, I was not able to wound him."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that mistakes are possible. It's just an omission. I am constantly being charged with the fact that I did have a weapon, but a hundred times later, I regretted the fact that I did not happen to have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's conclude. This statement does not bear your signature? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, why would somebody place your signature at the bottom of a statement which you are abiding by?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, you object?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry. They're asking this witness to speculate as to why someone else would commit forgery. It's not within his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You stated that you saw Stevo Arandjic at the court in Bijeljina for the first time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him personally before the war, Stevo. And during the war, the first time that I saw him during the war was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you in some kind of dispute with him before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that he was friendly with your brothers who were members of the Fourth Detachment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Stevo Arandjic reported you much later after that incident because he was good friends with your brother? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: It seems that -- unless I'm wrong -- would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Is seems to me that the witness is being asked to comment upon something that Stevo Arandjic did when his evidence has been repeatedly that he didn't see the -- Mr. Arandjic - I'm sorry - until whenever it was in 1994 that the trial took place in Bijeljina. Now, he's been fairly consistent about that, so what is the purpose of the question if this witness says that he didn't see him at all until trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understand. I will not ask this question. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because I was wondering how this witness would know if that report was made later and for what reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we agree that everything that is in this statement dated the 9th of November, 1992, except for the part referring to Stevo Arandjic, is it really what you stated in the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One last question about this. Where was your wife exchanged? Do you know the place where she was exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in Dragalici, via Croatia she went to Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I was wondering about these documents, the ID 24, the judgement of the court in Bijeljina, and this very statement of the SUP. Do you wish to tender them into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly, Your Honour. Yesterday we had only ID numbers given because there were no translations. Now I wish to tender them into evidence. And there is one more thing I've forgotten. With the Court's approval, I would like to ask the witness to sign his name on a blank piece of paper several times and for this also to be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm wondering about that latter part, the signature, because the witness has agreed that everything in this statement is correct except for the part regarding -- what is his name? Stevo Arandjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this statement is very important for me because of the credibility of this witness who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- made statements several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What I'm trying to say is you want to have the handwriting expert, I presume, when you're asking for his handwriting, just to say -- to prove whether or not -- or to show whether or not he actually signed this statement. Okay. May I have the Prosecution's stand on the -- first the admission of the two documents? MR. DI FAZIO: On that, could I address you after the afternoon break and give you the Prosecution's position on that. There's a matter regarding that that I want to speak to my learned colleagues about. I can you an answer immediately after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What is your position on these documents? MR. DI FAZIO: On that issue it's a fairly novel situation. I've not encountered it. May I have a moment to confer with my colleague, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: It seems -- it seems to me, if Your Honours please, the exercise is going to be pointless and -- unless it's conducted in such a way that an expert can say -- will meet whatever criterion an expert needs to be met in order to carry out an examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You see, the point is -- the contents of the statement, except for Stevo -- the one gentleman -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- have been agreed to by the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's just that he says he didn't sign it. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Now the issue of the signature, to prove the signature is a matter we can deal with at a later stage. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I take it that the Chamber is of the view that the signature should be taken at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, not at this stage, because you are yet to submit on it, because you were just asking to come back on the break. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What I'm saying is we can have the documents admitted and leave the issue of the signature on D22 still pending. I mean, right now, and then you can come back and make your submissions. MR. DI FAZIO: On the sample signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Whether or not he should provide samples or whether or not you want to do anything about it. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Well, my preference would be to address you on both of those issues immediately after the break, if I could have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. On both, whether or not you have any objection. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, the taking of samples from this witness in court, so we all know the document and we all know where the samples are, and (b), the question of the full admission into evidence of this document, the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What about the judgement? MR. DI FAZIO: -- About those two issues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What about the judgement, D24, the judgement of the court in Bijeljina? MR. DI FAZIO: There is no objection to that. I think the witness has effectively said he agrees with that

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So the -- no, no, no. The judgement in Bijeljina; that's what I'm talking about. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, he had no dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: I have got no objections to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Could we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D24/3 ter, and the English version D24/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And both are under seal because they contain the particulars of the witness. Now, Mr. Lukic you have finished your cross-examination except for perhaps replying to what the prosecution may say on the other document and the signature, so you will have that opportunity later. We will continue with the cross-examination by other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The next counsel. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Saric's defence, I will conduct the cross-examination of this witness. If you could bear just one second with me just to prepare my papers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Witness, while the counsel is getting his papers prepared, perhaps I would like to ask you one question on the court proceedings which took place in Bijeljina. In Bijeljina, sorry. Now, you said that Arandjic gave evidence. Did he give a statement or did he actually come to court and give evidence before the court in your presence? And if he did that, did you cross-examine him? Were you given the opportunity to cross-examine him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was in the courtroom, and he testified there, but I did not have the right to ask him anything. I had no rights. He made his statement, he finished it, and he left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Are you saying he spoke only or was the statement read by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He spoke. He made it orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel can proceed with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir. Witness, I will not address you by your name. Please don't take it as an insult. It is simply the usual procedure for protected witnesses. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic, and I will ask you questions on behalf of Mr. Simo Zaric. I will endeavour to put my questions to you simply and in a way that can be answered by "yes," "no," or, "I don't remember." If you do not understand any of my questions, please tell me so that I can reformulate them and put them in a different way. Mr. Lukic has already told you that you should wait for the question to be interpreted before you begin to reply, and you have also heard this from the Presiding Judge, Judge Mumba, but before I begin putting questions to you, on behalf of my client, I wish to express his regrets because of all the bad and difficult things that you, your family, and your brothers have gone through in Bosnia during the war. I will now begin my questioning. [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... line of questions that could possibly indicate some information about the witness. They are about his personal background and the personal background of some members of his family. So I believe that it would be appropriate to go in private session. As soon as I finish with this line of examination, I will inform the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go into private, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to move to a different topic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a topic that you've already testified about and a topic on which my learned friend Mr. Lukic already questioned you about, and it relates to the distribution of weapons. So I would also like to ask you a few questions about that. Amongst the people who were distributing the weapons in the TO building, was Ibrahim Salkic, called Ibela, amongst them too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him then at that time when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell me, were the weapons being distributed inside the TO building or in the courtyard of the TO building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw that through the gate, through the large TO door, they were being distributed outside in the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that Serb police officers upstairs in the police building were looking at that. They were watching. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The building across the street, is that a police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The Serb police officers who were watching, do they work at that police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So they were at their place of employment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if it's their place of employment to stand at the windows of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were these windows open?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me if it's true that on the first floor of the police station are the officers of the chief of SUP, the crime inspectors, as well as the commander of the police station, that these officers are on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The chief of the police station in Samac on the 16th of April was Dragan Lukac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Dragan Lukac was a criminal inspector in the crime sector but I think it was Vinko. I think his last name is Vinko Dragicevic from Hasici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, Dragan Lukac told us that at that time he was the chief of police, that shortly before that he was appointed to that post and this is why I was asking you specifically about that date, the 16th of April, when the weapons were distributed. But in any case, is Dragan Lukac a Croat by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And Vinko Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the commander of the police station at that time, was it Namik Suljic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Namik Suljic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ye.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May I have one second?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether Namik Suljic worked with the police? If you don't know whether he was a commander or not, at least did he work in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was a teacher at the high school, but also I saw him on the street in the uniform of a reserve police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that we will have to go to private session just briefly because again I will mention some names of the brothers of the witness and this could jeopardise his identity. J.MumbA: All right. Can we go into private session again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. We're discussing Fadil Topcagic. Did his whole -- was his whole face covered in paint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you then explain to us the parts of his face that were painted? His cheeks, his forehead? 2 A. His cheeks, his forehead. 3 Q. What about his cheek? What about his nose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. He couldn't have painted his lips. At least not at that time, his lips were not painted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to follow the chronology in your testimony so as not to confuse things. You testified that sometime around the 20th of April that you went to a meeting that was held in the Buducnost factory. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the meeting. All of us citizens from Bosanski Samac were told to go there, all people of military age and able to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I may have misused this word "meeting," but at any rate, I'm speaking about this event when everybody went to the Buducnost factory on the 20th of April because that's what happened then. You said that before you went there, your neighbour, Djoko Pisarevic, told you that you had to wear a white band. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you that only Muslims and Croats should wear that ribbon or did he just tell you that you should put it on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That Muslims and Croats should wear it. I don't think Djoko was wearing one of them. He was a Serb, so he didn't need to wear one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did Djoko tell you -- I'm trying to rephrase the question. Did he tell you that you personally should put on a band or did he tell you that there is an order that a band should be worn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that everybody needs to wear a band; there is an order to this effect. Muslims and Croats are to wear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any of the Serbs wear the band?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did soldiers wear a white band?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the arms where we wore them, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think my question was only whether -- whether they did wear a band or did not. This is the question that you need to respond to, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference in the way it's worn. The soldiers wore thin ribbons tied up here, and we had to tie broader bands around our arm. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please -- if Your Honours please, can the transcript indicate that when the witness was describing the "thin ribbons tied up here," and I quote directly from the transcript, he indicated a portion on his right -- his left arm near the elbow, part of the upper arm. I just think that ought to be put in the transcript. This sort of evidence could become important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. As the correct description where the arm -- where the band was worn. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did anybody set the width of the band that should be worn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether anybody ordered that this should be worn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I know that everybody did wear one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you heard about this from Djoko Pisarevic. You didn't receive any kind of notice or any information to this effect? Excuse me. Your answer was not registered by the transcript, so could you please repeat your answer to the last question. Concerning whether you heard about the obligation to wear the band from Djoko Pisarevic and to whether you received any kind of notice or information to this effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't receive anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Further on in your statement, you said that when you walked towards Buducnost you saw vehicles with the markings of the army of Republika Srpska. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more specific about these markings of the army of Republika Srpska. Where were they? Were they on the licence plates, on the tarpaulins, on the doors of the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the licence plates, VSR, and then the licence plate number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when was -- on what date was the army of Republika Srpska established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: A long time before the war broke out in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the 4th Detachment was also a part of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that it was not part of the JNA? I'm asking you once again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time I testified here, I said that it had nothing to do with the JNA, the real JNA. And I don't know about this kind -- this JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that your opinion, your conclusion, or is this relying on some facts that you know about the structure of the army of Republika Srpska, the international situation in Bosnia, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I see soldiers or an army where its members wear beards and they have cockades, then this is not, in my opinion, the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the information that the army of Republika Srpska was formed on the 12th of May, 1992, is not true, according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to move to this meeting, this gathering that was held in Buducnost. You said that the meeting was addressed by Jovo Savic. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before that meeting was held, did you know Jovo Savic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Jovo Savic lives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you know what he looks like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You were present at that meeting. Do you know in which capacity Jovo Savic was there? What was his position or his function in the army at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was deputy commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I won't put any more questions to you, then, concerning this meeting then. Just a few more questions about this. Did Jovo Savic wear a beard perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did he wear a tall hat with a cockade on his head or something similar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what kind of a uniform Jovo Savic had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were in Buducnost on that day, he wore an officers uniform, a regular SMB uniform, olive-grey uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was that the uniform that was worn in the JNA at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's move now to an event that happened after you left that meeting in front of the AS Cafe, and you described it in your statement here before this Tribunal. I would now like to ask you about some details concerning that event. What was the weather like at that time? Maybe I could help you. Was it cold that April and did it snow a couple of days before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it wasn't very cold. You could sit outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That event, when you were beaten up by two persons, what time of the day was it? Could you be more specific about the time of day that it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened around noon that day, between 11.00 and 12.00 noon. I can't say exactly what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I'm not insisting that you pinpoint the exact time. This event which you described in your first statement, which we have already referred to and which has been shown to you, and that's your statement given to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal on the 14th and the 17th of June, 1996, in that statement, you didn't say -- you didn't state that you saw Simo Zaric on that occasion. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I said that, but I did see him, and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about that statement of yours at that time. Did you state that you saw Simo Zaric at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I stated it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that my learned colleague from the Prosecutor could be of certain assistance like in the previous time when I had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just to get confirmation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, just for confirmation because it would be much quicker that our learned colleagues looked briefly through the statement, and they -- particularly on this portion of the statement when this incident is explained. So maybe we can do something about it, just to avoid that I show the whole statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is the statement of the 14th and 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: 14th and 17th of June, 1996, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And what exactly are you stating to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Going through this statement, I have noticed that the statement of my client, Mr. Zaric, was not mentioned in this incident, and it is the incident in front of Cafe AS on 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Having seen the statement, I can confirm that the witness certainly describes the episode. He describes the presence of Miroslav Tadic at the cafe on the -- during the episode and injuries he received, his subsequent hospitalisation, but as far as the episode is concerned, he makes no reference to Mr. Simo Zaric. Mr. Simo Zaric is certainly referred to later in the statement but in the context of other matters. And I couldn't fine my comments purely to the statement of the 14th and 17th of June, 1996. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has confirmed that Simo Zaric was not mentioned in relation to this incident when you provided this statement, i.e., your statement does not contain that information that Simo Zaric was present. Ten years have passed since then, as you have said, so I would like to ask you, has your recollection improved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So ten years later, you remember things better than you did then; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, then, what Simo Zaric was wearing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a military camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A camouflage military uniform. Well, that was my next question. I was expecting you to say that he was in a uniform, but I waited to see what kind of a uniform it was, and you've already responded to that. Then you said that during that incident when they were beating you, that Sumadinac and Cera who savagely beat you up, you said at one point you lost consciousness. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me how long you were unconscious?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't take a watch with me to see how long I was lying down. I have no idea how long I was lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know how long you were unconscious for. Did you see Simo Zaric before you lost consciousness or after you came to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I came to. After I recovered, I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see Simo Zaric at all until you regained -- until after you regained consciousness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they were beating me, I had to look down so that I couldn't look around to see who was coming in and out, in and out of the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know when Simo Zaric arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was there, but I don't know when he arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After that episode when you were forced to run to the SUP, you arrived at the police station and were told there that from that day on, you need to report to the SUP every morning. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me who issued this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mirko Pavic and five or six police officers were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But specifically who told you, "From tomorrow on, you have to report to the police station."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Mirko Pavic, but I can't really say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was Mirko Pavic's post in the police at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I think he was a deputy commander or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I won't insist on that. If you don't know, you don't know. According to your testimony, you continued to report to the SUP day after day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How long -- excuse me. I will rephrase my question. When you used to go to the SUP, what time of the day did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, around 8.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And while you were reporting to the SUP, how long would you stay at the SUP -- the -- at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to the SUP, I would report to the officer on duty and then he would note down the information that I had reported in, and after that, I returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, could you give us an estimate? How long did it take you from the moment you came in until the time you left the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes it took five minutes and sometimes it took one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Further on in your testimony, you stated that on one of those occasions when you reported to the SUP you saw Simo Zaric and that at that time, he told you when you didn't -- and did he tell you that when you didn't know how to be a gentleman, then you can be a slave? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, the interpreters are a little behind. Can you just wait?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'll wait for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell me, this event in the police station when Simo Zaric allegedly told you that, where exactly did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance to the police building there are -- there is a small staircase where the duty officer is, where there is a stall where he is. There is a double door a little further on. There was Seselj's picture, and we had to take a bow there first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Apart from Mr. Zaric and yourself, was there anyone else present at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't recall. I know that the duty police officer was there, Mr. Zaric, and myself. I was there to report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would have to bring you once again back to your interview given to the Office of the Prosecutor of the 13th of July, 1996. Did you on that occasion tell the Prosecutors that Simo Zaric had told you that since you didn't know how to be a gentleman, you now had to become a slave, that he told you that in Zasovica as you dug trenches? So is this how you described it to the Prosecutors on the 13th of July?
