utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you now what I said. I gave a lot of statements, and I don't remember to whom I said what. I had to give statements all over the place, to the police, but I do know now that this conversation took place in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to dwell on this a little more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANETLIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It seems to me that the witness mentioned, inter alia, police and Prosecution, tuzlusvo [phoen]. Maybe my learned friend can clarify that with witness, because we heard that impression. It was on line -- page 77, line 2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will definitely do that and thank you my dear colleague for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that the transcript does not reflect your words. You said that you had given statements -- a lot of statements. You mentioned the police and the Prosecution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to pinpoint the actual time when this event took place as you claim that it did. So it happened at the time when you were still reporting as ordered by Mirko Pavic to the police station every morning. Is that the time period we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So this happened before you started doing your work duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How did you then understand his remark about the slave? Because this was before the time when you were forced to go on work duty.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood it to mean that I -- I was on one side and my brothers were on the other side. If I had joined my brothers, I would not been here. I would not have been beaten up or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is your opinion on this issue? Do you believe that it would have happened if you had joined your brothers? I'm asking you to speculate perhaps, but this is -- in fact, I'm just asking you for your opinion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps this was a harder road, but I'm quite happy that I took it because it is easier for me. I would never have joined them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the sense of the remark -- the meaning of the remark was that this would not have happened if you had joined your brothers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I wonder whether you could seek from the witness a little clarification. This goes to the point raised by your colleague Mr. Pantelic and then confirmed by the witness that he said I gave statements to the police and the Prosecution. I would be interested to know which police and where.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will ask the witness again. Then I thought maybe you would ask me what Prosecutor he referred to, the Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal or some other Prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Williams wanted me to clarify some things with you, some details regarding this part of your testimony pertaining to when you said you had given a lot of statements to the police, to the Prosecution, and so on. She would like to know what police you're referring to. If there were several police forces involved, which ones, if you could specify. And what about the Prosecution? What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was exchanged in 1994, I gave a statement to the civilian police in Tuzla and to the military police. In 1994, I came to Gradacac, and I have gave a statement to the civilian police there. I met my family in July 1994, and I gave a statement to the police in Orasje, to the military police in Orasje. Also in Domaljevac I gave a statement to the civilian police. As regards the Prosecution, I referred to the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can proceed. Is this enough for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to go very briefly because we are running out of time. We don't have time to ask many more questions. This will refer to the beginning of your work duty or forced labour, depending on how you want to call it. In your testimony, you mentioned that you saw Simo Zaric on those occasions when you were in front of the SDK building and that he was just passing by and going upstairs to see Bozo Ninkovic. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The SDK building has the ground floor and the first floor; is that correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the ground floor there is just the public accounting office, the SDK as it was known at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Upstairs in that building there was the Secretariat for National Defence and the communication centre service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were in front of the building receiving your work assignment, as you said, you were in front of the building. You did not get into the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you were unable to see whether Simo Zaric went to the communications centre or to the Secretariat for National Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was thinking about moving to some other topic, and I believe that we are now to finish. It's 1800.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can continue tomorrow with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will continue tomorrow. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a few seconds, please. This witness mentioned that he gave a certain number of various statements to Bosnian police, Croatian police, et cetera. I would be very grateful if our learned friends, in this break until tomorrow, can check their records and maybe find some of these statements, because the well-known fact within this Tribunal is that the Prosecutor is in close connection with the security services, intelligence services, and police from Bosnia. So in other cases was the case probably. I'm not sure for this particular, but just -- because we have a witness here, maybe we could have some other angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANETLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecutor can find out whether they have anything and be able to tell us tomorrow. We will rise until tomorrow afternoon at 1415.
